newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania market regulator paves road to OTC.
newsitem.headline: Romania market regulator paves road to OTC.

text.p: Romania's CNVM capital market regulator said on Friday it had cleared the way for the launch of an over-the-counter (OTC) trading system by licensing its basic institutions.
The CNVM authorised a share registry and a depository, a clearing and settlement company and approved rules for their operation ahead of the start-up of the OTC market.

Romania's RASDAQ trading system was developed under a $21 million project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development and is modelled after the U.S. NASDAQ exchange. It is expected to start trading by end-September.

The OTC will eventually trade shares in some 4,000 companies included in a mass privatisation scheme under which some 15 million adult Romanians were offered 60 percent of those companies in exchange for vouchers and coupons.

The ambitious OTC scheme was delayed twice and analysts said Romania's poor infrastructure, hindering the linking of some 95 dealers and brokers in 300 workstations across the country, as well as problems in creating a share registry were the reasons for the delays.

Traders hail the kick-off of the OTC system as a welcome addition to the Bucharest stock exchange which has lost vigour in recent months and trades only 13 stocks. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
